hints: Look at the sampling days 4, 8, 12 and 16. Which of those four sampled cells must have come from the longest line of repeated mitosis?
Remember what happens to the TTAGGG telomere repeats in a normal body cell like a skin cell each time DNA is replicated for mitosis, when there is no telomerase to rebuild them.
walkthrough:
**Find the cell with the most divisions**

Think of this like a family tree starting from one cell. The longer you wait, the more rounds of mitosis have happened.

So the cell removed on day 16 has lived through more divisions than the cells removed on days 4, 8 or 12.

**Recall what mitosis does to telomeres**

Telomeres are protective TTAGGG repeats at the ends of chromosomes. In normal somatic cells, DNA polymerase cannot fully copy the very end of the lagging strand.

This is called the end replication problem, so a small piece of telomere is lost at every division and there is no telomerase to replace it.

**Pick the shortest telomere**

More divisions means more shortening. More shortening means fewer total bases left.

Out of 5548, 5580, 5645 and 5700, the smallest total is 5548. That must belong to the day 16 cell that divided the most.

options.A: Correct. 5548 is the smallest number of bases, so it shows the most shortening and therefore the most mitotic divisions.
options.B: Not correct. 5580 is longer than 5548, so this cell has lost less telomere and has undergone fewer divisions.
options.C: Not correct. 5645 is the second longest telomere, so this cell is from an earlier sampling time with fewer divisions.
options.D: Not correct. 5700 is the longest telomere, so it has shortened the least and belongs to the cell with the fewest divisions.
